# WithinHostExperiment

*Bioconductor Infrastructure for Within-Host Pathogen Variant QC,
Diversity, and Transmission Bottleneck Workflows*

[![Platforms](https://bioconductor.org/shields/availability/release/WithinHostExperiment.svg)](https://bioconductor.org/packages/WithinHostExperiment/)
[![Bioconductor devel
build](https://bioconductor.org/shields/build/devel/bioc/WithinHostExperiment.svg)](https://bioconductor.org/checkResults/devel/bioc-LATEST/WithinHostExperiment/)
[![DOI](https://img.shields.io/badge/DOI-10.18129%2FB9.bioc.WithinHostExperiment-blue.svg)](https://doi.org/10.18129/B9.bioc.WithinHostExperiment)
[![License:
Artistic-2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Artistic--2.0-blue.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/Artistic-2.0)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Why does this package exist?

Researchers studying within-host pathogen evolution run into four
practical problems:

1.  **Unreplicated iSNV calls include noise** – in the duplicate
    sequencing of Bendall *et al.* (2023), 53 of 159 calls (33%) differ
    by more than 2 percentage points between replicates (Figure 1).
2.  **Fragmented tooling** – importing from iVar, annotating genes,
    filtering, computing diversity and exporting for bottleneck
    estimation are often handled by separate scripts (Figure 3).
3.  **Longitudinal data need their own checks** – following variant
    frequencies across sampling days needs tracking and consistency
    flags that a single-sample workflow has no use for (Figure 4).
4.  **Hard filtering loses provenance** – deleting variants that fail a
    threshold prevents re-analysis under other criteria. Flagging
    instead keeps every call, while downstream summaries use only those
    that pass (Figures 1c, 6).

`WithinHostExperiment` brings these steps into one
`RangedSummarizedExperiment`-based container, from import through
replicate-aware QC, diversity and longitudinal summaries to export for
bottleneck estimation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Data sources

All figures use real, publicly available data:

| Source | Data | Role |
|----|----|----|
| **Bendall *et al.* (2023)** *Nat. Commun.* 14:272 | 159 iSNVs, 83 samples, duplicate sequencing, 132 transmission pairs | QC, diversity, transmission, population genetics (Figs 1–3, 5–6) |
| **Farjo *et al.* (2024)** *J. Virol.* 98:e01618-23 | Participant 432870: 9 daily saliva samples; the 6 that the study analysed (mean coverage of at least 1,000x; days 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8) are used | Longitudinal within-host evolution (Fig 4) |
| **NCBI RefSeq** NC_045512.2 | SARS-CoV-2 gene annotation (GFF3) and reference sequence (FASTA) | [`annotateGenes()`](reference/annotateGenes.md) (Fig 3b); [`annotateCodonChange()`](reference/annotateCodonChange.md), through [`VariantAnnotation::predictCoding()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/VariantAnnotation/man/predictCoding-methods.html), and the site counts of [`pNpSWithinHost()`](reference/pNpSWithinHost.md) (Fig 5b) |

Four files from the Bendall *et al.* call table ship inside the package,
in `inst/extdata`: both technical replicates of the donor and of the
recipient of household HH6, four of the study’s 159 calls, which the
vignette and the tests use as real data. The study’s repository states
no licence, so they are reproduced as a short excerpt attributed to the
paper and to the repository, and anyone wanting the data for their own
work should take them from the source. The Farjo *et al.* files used for
Figure 4 are kept only in the repository, not in the package, and come
from a repository released under the MIT licence. For the two NCBI
RefSeq files, NCBI states that it places no restrictions on the use or
distribution of the data in its molecular databases.
`inst/scripts/README.md` gives the provenance of every shipped file.

All figures were made with R version 4.6.1 by
`inst/scripts/generate_readme_figures.R`, which also writes every number
quoted below to `inst/scripts/readme_values/readme_figure_values.csv`;
the captions are filled from that file by `inst/scripts/fill_readme.R`,
which refuses to write a caption for a figure that run did not produce.
No data were simulated. Frequencies are those of replicate 1 throughout,
except in Figure 2, which bins the mean of the two replicates.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Problem 1: Unreplicated calls include noise

![Replicate-aware QC impact](reference/figures/fig1_replicate_qc.png)

> **Figure 1 \| Replicate-aware QC and post-hoc threshold exploration.**
> **(a)** Replicate frequencies for 159 iSNV calls: concordant
> (\|frequency difference\| \<= 2 percentage points, *n* = 106) and
> discordant (*n* = 53); R^2 = 0.948. That figure is carried by the
> spread across the whole range: among the calls below 10% mean
> frequency, where QC does its work, R^2 is 0.153. Across all calls, the
> median difference between replicates is 1.1 percentage points. **(b)**
> Per-sample nucleotide diversity before (naive) and after replicate QC;
> black diamonds mark the medians (0.096 and 0.038 x 10^-4). QC only
> removes calls, so pi cannot rise. It left pi untouched in most samples
> and lowered it in 38 of 83, by a median of 88% among those; in 18
> samples no call survived and pi fell to zero. **(c)** Median pi as the
> concordance threshold varies from 0 to 20 percentage points of
> replicate difference, recomputed from the replicate frequencies
> already in the object rather than by re-importing and re-filtering the
> data; the dashed lines mark 2 and 5 percentage points.

![iSNV frequency
spectrum](reference/figures/fig2_frequency_spectrum.png)

> **Figure 2 \| Where discordant calls fall.** Mean replicate
> frequencies of the 159 calls, which fall at 146 distinct variants
> (position and substitution). Discordance is not confined to the
> low-frequency band where sequencing and amplification errors are
> hardest to tell apart from genuine minority variants: 18 of the 53
> discordant calls sit below 10% (34%), against 62 of the 106 concordant
> ones (58%), so replicates disagree more often at intermediate
> frequencies than at the bottom of the range. Part of that is the rule
> itself: a fixed tolerance in percentage points removes more calls
> where the sampling spread of the difference is wider, as Figure 6b
> sets out.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Problem 2: One package, complete workflow

![From data to annotated transmission
pairs](reference/figures/fig3_qc_overview.png)

> **Figure 3 \| From raw data to annotated transmission pairs.** **(a)**
> Mean read depth, averaged over the two replicates, for all 188
> sequenced samples (median 2,033x); the 83 samples that carry at least
> one iSNV call, and that every other panel uses, are a subset of them.
> **(b)** Concordant iSNV calls by gene, annotated with
> [`annotateGenes()`](reference/annotateGenes.md) from the gene records
> of the NCBI GFF3, read with `rtracklayer::import()`. **(c)** Pair
> HH17_K, the pair with the most concordant donor iSNVs among those
> whose recipient carries calls of its own: 3 of 3 donor iSNVs have no
> call in the recipient, which carries 2 of its own. **(d)** Of the 52
> pairs whose donor carried at least one concordant iSNV (132 pairs in
> the metadata), 47 (90%) share none with the recipient. Two limits
> matter for reading this panel. Recipient calls are limited to
> frequencies of 2–98%, so a donor variant that became fixed in the
> recipient also counts as not shared; and in 26 of these pairs the
> recipient carries no iSNV call at all, so absence of data is recorded
> here as absence of sharing. The panel describes detection and is not a
> bottleneck estimate (Bendall *et al.* 2023 report those).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Problem 3: Longitudinal tracking needs infrastructure

![Longitudinal within-host
dynamics](reference/figures/fig4_diversity_landscape.png)

> **Figure 4 \| Within-host dynamics across sampling days.** Daily
> saliva samples from one SARS-CoV-2 participant (Farjo *et al.* 2024),
> limited to the 6 samples the study analysed (days 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8); a
> call needs at least 1,000 reads and a frequency between 3% and 97%.
> The iVar tables also list insertions and deletions; 909 such rows are
> dropped and the 1,252 substitution rows kept, so every count below is
> of iSNVs. **(a)** Richness (bars) and pi (line): QC-passed iSNVs peak
> at 141 on day 8, and pi peaks on day 8. **(b)** Frequency trajectories
> of the 10 variants with the widest frequency range, tracked with
> [`trackFrequency()`](reference/trackFrequency.md); the dotted line
> marks the 3% threshold. **(c)** Folded spectra from
> [`buildSFS()`](reference/buildSFS.md) on the first, peak and last
> sampled days, which here are days 1, 8; two of them coincide when the
> peak falls on the first or last day sampled. **(d)**
> [`flagTemporalInconsistency()`](reference/flagTemporalInconsistency.md):
> 288 of 294 variant sites (98%) are detected on a single day. A site
> can also be missed on a day when its depth is below 1,000 reads, or
> when its frequency leaves the 3–97% window, so a variant that goes to
> fixation is counted the same way; transient sites are flagged for
> review rather than treated as errors.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Evolutionary summaries from the same flagged data

![Population-genetic
summaries](reference/figures/fig5_evolutionary_analysis.png)

> **Figure 5 \| Population-genetic summaries of the flagged data.**
> **(a)** Tajima’s D for the 10 samples carrying at least three
> concordant iSNVs, using read depth capped at 100 as the sample size:
> median -0.32, 60% below zero. They are the minority: of the 65 samples
> with any concordant call, 41 carry one (63%) and 14 carry two. Below
> three segregating sites D is a function of one or two frequencies
> rather than a description of a spectrum, so
> [`tajimaD()`](reference/tajimaD.md) returns `NA` and those samples are
> absent from the panel. Calls below the 2% frequency threshold are
> absent, and negative D is expected both under purifying selection and
> after population growth, so these values describe the spectra rather
> than test either. **(b)** Within-host pN/pS, the ratio of
> nonsynonymous to synonymous iSNVs per site with sites counted by the
> method of Nei and Gojobori (1986), pooling concordant calls across
> samples (50 nonsynonymous, 49 synonymous; pooled ratio 0.29). A
> further 7 concordant calls lie outside the annotated coding sequences,
> or carry no codon annotation, and enter neither count. These are
> counts of polymorphism within hosts rather than of substitutions
> between them, so the ratio is a pN/pS, computed by
> [`pNpSWithinHost()`](reference/pNpSWithinHost.md) with no multiple-hit
> correction. The panel shows the 8 genes with at least two counted
> calls and a defined ratio, leaving out 1; those ratios rest on a
> handful of calls and are given with their counts. None of them is
> evidence of selection on any gene. **(c)** Per-sample pi ranked by the
> naive estimate; segments show the reduction from QC. **(d)** Naive, QC
> and bias-corrected spectra as `WithinHostSFS` objects from
> [`buildSFS()`](reference/buildSFS.md) and
> [`correctSFSBias()`](reference/correctSFSBias.md) (binomial
> correction). The correction reweights bins by the chance of observing
> a variant at that frequency given the depth; at this depth every bin
> is far above the detection limit, so it changes 0 bins and the
> corrected series lies under the QC one.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Problem 4: QC should remove noise, not signal

![What replicate QC
changes](reference/figures/fig6_consensus_validation.png)

> **Figure 6 \| What replicate QC changes.** **(a)** Tajima’s D before
> and after QC in the 10 samples carrying at least three calls both
> before and after: median -0.32 before QC and -0.32 after. QC removed
> no call from most of them, so it changed D in 3, where the median
> change is -0.09; so few values admit no distribution-free 95%
> interval, which needs at least six. Over all 10 the median change is
> 0.00, with a 95% interval of -0.09 to 0.00 from binomial order
> statistics: the unchanged samples outnumber the rest, so the interval
> sits against zero and carries little information about the size of the
> change. A further 6 samples leave the comparison because QC left them
> fewer than three calls, so they have no D after QC. **(b)** Frequency
> spectra of the calls QC kept and the calls it removed (86 and 49 of
> them fall inside the binned frequency range), compared with
> [`compareSFS()`](reference/compareSFS.md): chi-squared = 10.3, df = 9,
> asymptotic *p* = 0.327 and Monte Carlo *p* from 10^5 tables = 0.332;
> the smallest expected count is 0.7. Two things keep this descriptive:
> calls pooled across samples are not independent draws, and the
> concordance rule is a fixed 2-percentage-point tolerance on a
> difference whose sampling spread grows with frequency, so the two
> groups would differ in shape to some degree even if every call were
> genuine.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Installation

``` r

# After Bioconductor acceptance:
if (!require("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("WithinHostExperiment")

# Development version from GitHub. Not recommended: it is not the version
# Bioconductor builds and checks, and it can change between commits.
BiocManager::install("CuiweiG/WithinHostExperiment")
```

## Quick start

``` r

library(WithinHostExperiment)

# 1. Import donor and recipient VCFs, with the reference they were called
#    against so that the genome length is recorded on the object
vcf_d <- system.file("extdata", "test_donor.vcf",
    package = "WithinHostExperiment")
vcf_r <- system.file("extdata", "test_recipient.vcf",
    package = "WithinHostExperiment")
ref <- Biostrings::readDNAStringSet(system.file("extdata", "test_ref.fa",
    package = "WithinHostExperiment"))
whe <- readWithinHost(c(vcf_d, vcf_r), genome = ref,
    colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(
        sample_id = c("donor", "recipient"),
        role      = c("donor", "recipient"),
        pair_id   = c("pair_1", "pair_1")),
    caller = "ivar")

# 2. QC -- flag, don't delete
whe <- flagISNV(whe, ISNVFilter(minDepth = 200L, minFreq = 0.03))

# 3. Diversity (finite-sample corrected pi, per site of the recorded genome)
div <- calcDiversity(passedISNV(whe))

# 4. Transmission bottleneck
nb <- quickBottleneck(whe, pairId = "pair_1")
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Key design principles

1.  **Flag, don’t delete.** QC marks variants in `qcPass` rather than
    removing rows, preserving all data for re-analysis under different
    thresholds.
2.  **Replicate-aware.** Technical replicate concordance is part of the
    QC step rather than a separate script.
3.  **Interoperable, don’t reinvent.** Standardised export to
    ViralBottleneck (Zheng *et al.* 2025) and VRanges-based Bioconductor
    workflows.
4.  **Bioconductor-native.** Built on `RangedSummarizedExperiment`;
    subsetting, combining, and accessors follow Bioconductor
    conventions.

## Relationship to existing tools

| Tool | Role | Relationship |
|----|----|----|
| iVar, LoFreq, Freebayes | Variant calling | Upstream – we import their output |
| deepSNV | Low-frequency variant detection | Upstream – complementary |
| ViralBottleneck | Bottleneck estimation (6 methods) | Downstream – we export to it; also self-contained via [`exactBottleneck()`](reference/exactBottleneck.md) |
| QSutils | Quasispecies diversity | Parallel – different granularity (haplotype vs iSNV) |
| CliqueSNV, ShoRAH | Haplotype phasing | Complementary – their output can feed into WHE |

## Reproducibility

All README figures are generated from public data by one script, and the
captions are then filled from the values it records:

``` r

# Clone the repository, then from the package root directory:
source("inst/scripts/generate_readme_figures.R")
source("inst/scripts/fill_readme.R")
```

`inst/scripts/reproduce_all.R` runs the whole chain from the raw data:
the Bendall *et al.* excerpts, the synthetic fixtures, the example
dataset, an install of the source, the test suite, the figures, this
README and the functional checks, each in its own R process, and reports
whether every derived file came out as committed.

``` r

# From the package root of a clone:
system2(file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript"), "inst/scripts/reproduce_all.R")
```

Data files in `inst/scripts/real_data/` (GitHub only, not in installed
package):

| File | Source | Description |
|----|----|----|
| `all_variants_filtered.tsv` | Bendall *et al.* 2023 | 159 iSNV calls, 83 samples, both replicates |
| `AvgCoverage.all` | Bendall *et al.* 2023 | Per-replicate mean amplicon depth |
| `Transmission_pairs.csv` | Bendall *et al.* 2023 | Household transmission pair metadata |
| `farjo_longitudinal/` | Farjo *et al.* 2024 | Daily saliva iVar TSVs for participant 432870, with `samples_432870.csv` (dates, coverage and study inclusion, built by `inst/scripts/prepare_farjo_metadata.R` from github.com/BROOKELAB/SARS-CoV-2-within-host-evolution) |
| `sars2_NC045512.gff3` | NCBI RefSeq | SARS-CoV-2 gene annotation (NC_045512.2) |
| `sars2_NC045512.fasta` | NCBI RefSeq | Reference sequence (NC_045512.2), read with [`Biostrings::readDNAStringSet()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/Biostrings/man/XStringSet-io.html) and passed to [`pNpSWithinHost()`](reference/pNpSWithinHost.md), which takes each call’s codons from [`annotateCodonChange()`](reference/annotateCodonChange.md), for Figure 5b |
| `MHM*_rep*.tsv`, `all_variants_filtered_unmerged.tsv` | Bendall *et al.* 2023 | Per-sample iVar tables and the pre-merge call table, kept as provenance for the merged file above; the figure script reads neither |
| `farjo_longitudinal/user_432870.csv` | Farjo *et al.* 2024 | The study’s own per-SNP summary for this participant, kept for comparison; not read by the figure script |

## Key references

- Farjo M *et al.* (2024) Within-host evolutionary dynamics and tissue
  compartmentalization during acute SARS-CoV-2 infection. *J. Virol.*
  98:e01618-23.
- Roder AE *et al.* (2023) Optimized quantification of intra-host viral
  diversity in SARS-CoV-2 and influenza virus sequence data. *mBio*
  14:e01046-23.
- Bendall EE *et al.* (2023) Rapid transmission and tight bottlenecks
  constrain the evolution of highly transmissible SARS-CoV-2 variants.
  *Nat. Commun.* 14:272.
- Sobel Leonard A *et al.* (2017) Transmission bottleneck size
  estimation from pathogen deep-sequencing data, with an application to
  human influenza A virus. *J. Virol.* 91:e00171-17.
- Mostefai F *et al.* (2024) Refining SARS-CoV-2 intra-host variation by
  leveraging large-scale sequencing data. *NAR Genom. Bioinform.*
  6:lqae145.
- Zheng B, Johnson PCD, Hughes J (2025) ViralBottleneck: an R package
  for estimating viral transmission bottlenecks from deep sequencing
  data using multiple methods. *Virus Evol.* 11:veaf071.
- Tajima F (1989) Statistical method for testing the neutral mutation
  hypothesis by DNA polymorphism. *Genetics* 123:585-595.
- Fu YX (1997) Statistical tests of neutrality of mutations against
  population growth, hitchhiking and background selection. *Genetics*
  147:915-925.
- Nei M, Gojobori T (1986) Simple methods for estimating the numbers of
  synonymous and nonsynonymous substitutions. *Mol. Biol. Evol.*
  3:418-426.

# Package index

## Package

An overview of the package, its classes and its workflow.

- [`WithinHostExperiment-package`](WithinHostExperiment-package.md) :
  WithinHostExperiment: Within-Host Pathogen Variant QC, Diversity, and
  Bottleneck

## Classes

The container for within-host variant calls, the filter that QC applies
to it, the rule technical replicates must meet, and the site frequency
spectrum built from the calls.

- [`show(`*`<WithinHostExperiment>`*`)`](WithinHostExperiment-class.md)
  [`` `[`( ``*`<WithinHostExperiment>`*`,`*`<ANY>`*`,`*`<ANY>`*`,`*`<ANY>`*`)`](WithinHostExperiment-class.md)
  : WithinHostExperiment: Container for within-host pathogen variant
  data
- [`show(`*`<ISNVFilter>`*`)`](ISNVFilter-class.md) : ISNVFilter:
  Quality control filter for iSNV analysis
- [`show(`*`<ConcordanceRule>`*`)`](ConcordanceRule-class.md) :
  ConcordanceRule: agreement required between technical replicates
- [`show(`*`<WithinHostSFS>`*`)`](WithinHostSFS-class.md) :
  WithinHostSFS: Site Frequency Spectrum for within-host variants

## Import and conversion

Build the container from VCF files, variant tables or Bioconductor
objects, combine objects, and convert back.

- [`WithinHostExperiment()`](WithinHostExperiment.md) : Create a
  WithinHostExperiment from components
- [`readWithinHost()`](readWithinHost.md) : Import iSNV data from VCF
  files
- [`readWithinHostTable()`](readWithinHostTable.md) : Import iSNV data
  from tabular files
- [`coerce-WHE`](coerce-WHE.md)
  [`coerce,WithinHostExperiment,data.frame-method`](coerce-WHE.md)
  [`coerce,WithinHostExperiment,VRanges-method`](coerce-WHE.md)
  [`coerce,VRanges,WithinHostExperiment-method`](coerce-WHE.md)
  [`coerce,VCF,WithinHostExperiment-method`](coerce-WHE.md) : Convert
  between WithinHostExperiment, data.frame, VRanges and VCF
- [`combineRows(`*`<WithinHostExperiment>`*`)`](WHE-combine.md)
  [`combineCols(`*`<WithinHostExperiment>`*`)`](WHE-combine.md) :
  Combine WithinHostExperiment objects by rows or columns
- [`example_whe`](example_whe.md) : Example WithinHostExperiment dataset

## Accessors

The QC audit log, the filters applied, the calls that passed, and the
transmission pairs described by the sample metadata.

- [`qcLog()`](WHE-accessors.md) [`qcFilters()`](WHE-accessors.md)
  [`passedISNV()`](WHE-accessors.md)
  [`transmissionPairs()`](WHE-accessors.md)
  [`` `qcLog<-`() ``](WHE-accessors.md)
  [`` `qcFilters<-`() ``](WHE-accessors.md) : Access the QC audit log

## Quality control

Choose filters and flag, without deleting, calls that fail depth,
frequency, strand, primer or replicate criteria; report likely
cross-contamination and summarise what QC removed.

- [`ISNVFilter()`](ISNVFilter.md) : Create an ISNVFilter object
- [`ConcordanceRule()`](ConcordanceRule.md) : Create a ConcordanceRule
  object
- [`adaptiveFilter()`](adaptiveFilter.md) : Create a
  technology-appropriate ISNVFilter
- [`flagISNV()`](flagISNV.md) : Flag iSNV sites based on quality
  criteria
- [`flagPrimerSites()`](flagPrimerSites.md) : Flag iSNVs in primer
  binding regions
- [`flagReplicateDiscordance()`](flagReplicateDiscordance.md) : Flag
  iSNVs with replicate discordance
- [`sciStrandBias()`](sciStrandBias.md) : Strand Coverage Imbalance
  (SCI) score
- [`flagStrandBiasSCI()`](flagStrandBiasSCI.md) : Flag strand-biased
  iSNVs using the SCI metric
- [`detectCrossContamination()`](detectCrossContamination.md) : Detect
  potential cross-contamination between samples
- [`qcSummary()`](qcSummary.md) : Generate a QC summary report

## Annotation

Label sites with genes and with the codon and amino acid change each
substitution makes.

- [`annotateGenes()`](annotateGenes.md) : Label variant sites with the
  genes they overlap
- [`annotateCodonChange()`](annotateCodonChange.md) : Codon and amino
  acid consequence of each SNV

## Diversity

Per-sample diversity indices, their comparison between groups, a
plausibility check, and a model of diversity against covariates.

- [`calcDiversity()`](calcDiversity.md) : Compute within-host diversity
  indices
- [`compareDiversity()`](compareDiversity.md) : Compare diversity
  between sample groups
- [`checkDiversityPlausibility()`](checkDiversityPlausibility.md) :
  Check diversity estimates against heuristic plausibility ranges
- [`shannonISNV()`](shannonISNV.md) : Shannon entropy from iSNV
  frequencies
- [`piISNV()`](piISNV.md) : Nucleotide diversity (pi) from iSNV
  frequencies
- [`wattersonISNV()`](wattersonISNV.md) : Watterson's theta from iSNV
  count
- [`simpsonISNV()`](simpsonISNV.md) : Simpson diversity index for iSNV
  frequencies
- [`chao1ISNV()`](chao1ISNV.md) : Chao1 richness estimator for iSNV data
- [`fitDiversityModel()`](fitDiversityModel.md) : Fit a linear model to
  diversity data

## Site frequency spectrum

Bin allele frequencies into a spectrum, correct it for the detection
threshold, compare spectra and compute statistics from one.

- [`buildSFS()`](buildSFS.md) : Build a site frequency spectrum from a
  WithinHostExperiment
- [`buildSFSList()`](buildSFSList.md) : Build SFS for all samples in a
  WithinHostExperiment
- [`correctSFSBias()`](correctSFSBias.md) : Correct ascertainment bias
  in the within-host SFS
- [`compareSFS()`](compareSFS.md) : Compare two within-host SFS objects
- [`neutralityFromSFS()`](neutralityFromSFS.md) : Compute all neutrality
  statistics from a WithinHostSFS

## Neutrality and selection

Tajima’s D and Fu’s Fs, the within-host pN/pS ratio, consensus sequences
for between-host dN/dS, and selection coefficients from frequency
change.

- [`calcNeutralityTests()`](calcNeutralityTests.md) : Compute neutrality
  test statistics
- [`tajimaD()`](tajimaD.md) : Tajima's D statistic
- [`fusFs()`](fusFs.md) : Fu's Fs statistic
- [`pNpSWithinHost()`](pNpSWithinHost.md) : Within-host pN/pS ratio
- [`consensusSequences()`](consensusSequences.md) : Consensus sequence
  of each sample
- [`estimateSelectionCoefficient()`](estimateSelectionCoefficient.md) :
  Estimate selection coefficient from frequency trajectory

## Transmission

Shared and private variants of a donor-recipient pair, bottleneck size
estimates, and exports for other bottleneck tools.

- [`calcSharedVariants()`](calcSharedVariants.md) : Calculate shared
  variant statistics
- [`quickBottleneck()`](quickBottleneck.md) : Quick bottleneck size
  estimation (beta-binomial approximate MLE)
- [`exactBottleneck()`](exactBottleneck.md) : Exact bottleneck size
  estimation
- [`exportPairFrequencies()`](exportPairFrequencies.md) : Export
  donor-recipient frequency table
- [`asViralBottleneckInput()`](asViralBottleneckInput.md) : Export data
  for ViralBottleneck package

## Longitudinal

Follow variant frequencies through the samples of one host over time,
and flag sites seen at too few timepoints.

- [`trackFrequency()`](trackFrequency.md) : Track variant frequency
  trajectories over time
- [`detectEmergingVariants()`](detectEmergingVariants.md) : Detect
  emerging variants across time points
- [`flagTemporalInconsistency()`](flagTemporalInconsistency.md) : Flag
  temporally inconsistent iSNVs in longitudinal data

## Multi-caller

Combine and compare the calls of several variant callers on the same
samples.

- [`consensusISNV()`](consensusISNV.md) : Multi-caller consensus iSNV
  detection
- [`calcCallerConcordance()`](calcCallerConcordance.md) : Pairwise
  caller concordance matrix
- [`benchmarkCallers()`](benchmarkCallers.md) : Benchmark variant
  callers against truth or each other

## Statistics

Permutation tests and multiple-testing correction for the summaries
above.

- [`permutationTest()`](permutationTest.md) : Permutation test for
  two-group comparison
- [`multitestCorrection()`](multitestCorrection.md) : Multiple testing
  correction for p-values

## Visualisation

Frequency spectra of an object or of WithinHostSFS objects,
donor-recipient scatter plots, a QC dashboard and frequency
trajectories.

- [`plotFrequencySpectrum()`](plotFrequencySpectrum.md) : Plot iSNV
  frequency spectrum
- [`plotPairScatter()`](plotPairScatter.md) : Plot donor-recipient
  frequency scatter
- [`plotQCDashboard()`](plotQCDashboard.md) : QC dashboard plot
- [`plotSFS()`](plotSFS.md) : Plot a within-host site frequency spectrum
- [`plotFrequencyTrajectory()`](plotFrequencyTrajectory.md) : Plot
  allele frequency trajectories over time
